What We Believe

Our Investment Philosophy

At LiveWell Capital, our investment philosophy is built on four foundational pillars that guide every portfolio decision. We believe in a goals-based approach that prioritizes diversification, allows for tactical adjustments, and maximizes tax efficiency — all within a holistic wealth management framework.

Personalized Wealth Management

Our approach brings together goal-based financial planning and portfolio management under a unified tax and estate planning strategy. The intersection of these disciplines is where true personalized wealth management happens — tailored to each client's unique circumstances, goals, and values.

★

Goal Based

Any money need for shorter-term goals needs to be safe, secure, and relatively liquid (cash and cash alternatives). Longer-term goals can take more risk for higher expected returns.

◎

Diversified

We use different asset classes (Large Cap, Mid Cap, Small Cap, International, Alternatives, etc.) to spread risk and capture returns across the full market.

↕

Tactical

Our team may tilt up or down (overweight or underweight) certain asset classes as our research dictates, adapting to changing market conditions.

☑

Tax-Efficient

Our team deploys a range of strategies designed to reduce capital gains, income, state, and estate taxes throughout the portfolio.

Goals-Based Portfolio Structure

We structure portfolios across three time horizons, each with a distinct purpose and return target. This time-weighted asset location approach ensures the right investments are matched to the right goals.

Short Term Portfolio
Time Horizon: Year 1–7
Allocation: Cash (1–2 years), Short-term Fixed Income (5–6 years)
Liquidity: 100%
Goal Returns: 3–5%
Core Portfolio
Time Horizon: Years 8–15
Allocation: 70% Equity, 30% Fixed Income
Objective: Income and Growth
Goal Returns: 6–8%
Long Term Portfolio
Time Horizon: Years 16+
Allocation: 90–100% Equity
Objective: Long-Term Growth
Goal Returns: 8+%

Is Now a Good Time to Look Beyond U.S. Large Cap?

The S&P 500's forward P/E of 21x sits well above its 10-year average of 18.7x, while international developed markets (MSCI EAFE) trade at just 16.5x — a 25% discount. MSCI EAFE Small Cap and Emerging Markets offer even deeper value at 13x and 12.5x respectively. Meanwhile, top 10 stock concentration has surpassed dot-com era peaks, creating concentration risk.

The Case for Diversification

The S&P 500's elevated valuation (21x vs 18.7x average) and extreme concentration (top 10 stocks >40%) create risks that warrant proactive diversification into international developed markets trading at a 25% discount.

How Our Allocation Has Changed Over Time (2018–2024)

Our tactical approach has evolved significantly. In 2018, we were overweight U.S. Large Cap and International Developed. By 2024, we shifted to underweight U.S. Large Cap while moving to overweight U.S. Mid Cap and U.S. Small Cap. Emerging Markets moved from overweight to underweight. This demonstrates our commitment to active tactical management — we don't set it and forget it.

3rd Party Research: BlackRock Capital Market Forecast (2025–2035)

BlackRock's 10-year capital market projections reinforce our allocation philosophy. Private Credit (Direct Lending) is expected to deliver 10.60% annualized returns, and Private Equity (Buyout) 12.40% — significantly outpacing public market alternatives. International equity (7.40%) and Emerging Markets (7.80%) are projected to outperform U.S. equities (5.20%), supporting our tactical tilt toward international diversification.

3rd Party Research: PGIM — Valuation & Yield Regimes

PGIM's research shows that starting valuations have a powerful impact on forward 10-year returns. Stocks starting at P/E ratios above 23x have historically delivered just 3.80% annualized over the following decade — and we're currently at 21x. Meanwhile, bonds starting at 4–6% yields (where we are now) have historically delivered 5.20% annualized. This research supports our balanced, diversified approach.

How We Execute

Optimization satellites — additions to the core portfolio

Our execution framework goes well beyond basic asset allocation. We layer four optimization satellites on top of each client's core portfolio, addressing tax efficiency, performance enhancement, income generation, and charitable giving. This comprehensive approach ensures every aspect of a client's financial life is coordinated and optimized.

The 7 Drivers of Investment Outcomes

Research shows that the top 5 drivers of investment outcomes are entirely within your control. Investor behavior, stock-to-bond ratio, tax strategy, planning strategy, and underlying fees matter far more than equity class weighting or security selection. This is the foundation of our approach — we focus on what we can control.

Optimization Satellites in Practice

Each satellite adds a specific layer of value to the core portfolio. Tax Optimization uses direct indexing and algorithmic tax-loss harvesting to capture losses that offset gains. Performance Optimization adds private investments for return enhancement and diversification. Income Optimization builds bond ladders and protected income layers. Charitable Giving Optimization structures DAFs and charitable trusts for tax-efficient giving.

Core Portfolio
Diversified asset allocation across equity, fixed income, and alternatives. The foundation that every optimization satellite builds upon.
Tax Optimization
Direct indexing and algorithmic tax-loss harvesting to capture losses that offset gains, reducing the tax drag on portfolio returns.
Performance Optimization
Private investments including private credit, private equity, and real assets for return enhancement and diversification beyond public markets.
Income Optimization
Bond ladders, protected income layers, and distribution-focused strategies to generate reliable cash flow for retirement and income needs.
Charitable Giving Optimization
Donor-advised funds (DAFs) and charitable trusts structured for tax-efficient giving, enabling clients to support causes while minimizing tax impact.

Maverick NEW

Rides the winners — with a safety net

Systematic momentum with drawdown defense. The Maverick strategy combines a momentum sleeve of individual equities with a diversified completion sleeve of ETFs. A drawdown overlay actively manages risk by reducing equity exposure when market conditions deteriorate, providing a built-in safety net that traditional buy-and-hold strategies lack.

Model portfolio performance — not composite performance of actual client accounts. See disclosures below.

How It Works

The Maverick strategy employs a dual-sleeve approach:

  • Momentum Sleeve: 29 individual stocks selected via a systematic momentum ranking. The model identifies the strongest relative-strength equities across sectors and holds them until their momentum fades, rotating into new leaders at each rebalance.
  • Completion Sleeve: Diversified ETFs covering bonds (IUSB, BNDX), international equity (IXUS), US extended market (VXF), managed futures (DBMF), and government cash (DGCXX). This provides broad market exposure and risk dampening.
  • Drawdown Defense Overlay: When market breadth deteriorates or trend signals turn negative, the overlay systematically reduces equity exposure, moving to cash to protect against deep drawdowns. This is what separates Maverick from pure momentum strategies.

Back-Tested Track Record (2007-Present)

16Annual wins vs SPY
3Annual losses vs SPY
19 years tested

Maverick's momentum + drawdown defense has outperformed the S&P 500 in 16 of 19 calendar years, including during major bear markets like 2008 and 2020.

Neo NEW

Maximized risk-adjusted returns

Rules-based ETF rotation. Neo employs a systematic tactical rotation across 8 ETF pairs, selecting the stronger-performing ETF from each pair on a monthly basis using relative strength signals. This disciplined, emotion-free approach captures returns across growth, trend, factor, global, macro, AI, sector, and cycle themes.

Model portfolio performance — not composite performance of actual client accounts. See disclosures below.

How It Works

The Neo strategy rotates across 8 ETF pairs, each representing a different market theme:

  • Monthly Rotation: At each monthly rebalance, the model compares the relative strength of each ETF pair and selects the stronger performer. This ensures the portfolio is always tilted toward the prevailing market leadership.
  • Theme Diversification: The 8 pairs span growth (SPY/QQQ), trend (VOOG/DBMF), factor (SPMO/SPLV), global (ACWI/ACWV), macro (PHYS/BTC), AI chain (XLC/PSI), sector (XBI/PPA), and cycle (XLE/IWY) — providing exposure across distinct return drivers.
  • Rules-Based Discipline: No discretionary overrides. The model executes its rotation rules consistently, removing emotional bias from investment decisions.

Alternatives

Private credit, private equity, and real assets

Private credit, private equity, and real assets offerings available within the LiveWell Capital platform. Click any card to expand detailed performance, terms, and metrics. Fact sheets link to SharePoint.

The Benefits of Private Credit

Private credit deserves a place in modern portfolios due to structural advantages, market growth, and performance stability.

CFA Institute

Private credit has evolved into a major source of corporate financing, now a $2.6 trillion global market.

CAIA Association

Offers portfolio diversification, potential for higher alpha, less market efficiency, and contractual cash flows.

McKinsey & Company

Return dispersion remained the narrowest of all private market asset classes, offering consistent performance.

BlackRock

Provides higher income and return potential, structural protections, and diversification.

Hamilton Lane

Offers downside protection via senior secured debt positioning at the top of the capital structure.

BIS

Firms borrowing from private credit funds value flexible loan terms and are often underserved by banks.

Private Credit vs. Public High Yield: The Illiquidity Premium

Private credit has historically delivered a 2.5–4.0% annual illiquidity premium over public high yield, compensating investors for reduced liquidity with higher income, structural protections, and lower return dispersion. Third-party estimates: Cliffwater (~3.5% long-run), BlackRock (4.2% 10-yr avg), NISA (2.6–3.7%).

The Benefits of Private Equity

Private equity enhances long-term portfolio growth through operational value creation, access to privately held companies, and market inefficiency.

Bain & Company

Buyout managers generate operational value rather than relying strictly on financial leverage.

Blackstone

Manager capabilities such as go-to-market strategy and technological innovation build business value over time.

CFA Institute

Private markets have expanded to more than $18 trillion in global AUM, representing a systemic inflection point.

McKinsey & Company

"Alpha is less likely to emerge from market dynamics alone. Increasingly, it will be made."

BlackRock

Diversification through expanded opportunity set and structural protections.

CAIA Association

Higher alpha through less efficient markets and active management.

Private Equity vs. Public Equities: The Illiquidity Premium

Private equity has historically delivered a 2–3% annual illiquidity premium over public equities, rewarding long-term investors with access to privately negotiated deals, operational value creation, and reduced mark-to-market volatility. Third-party estimates: Cliffwater (4.8% over 23 years), AQR (2.3% over 31 years).

Our Fees

Transparent, competitive, and aligned with client success

Our fee structure is designed to be fair and competitive at every asset level. Once client assets reach $500,000, we significantly reduce fees because additional assets do not add complexity at the same rate at which many fee structures charge.

Fee Philosophy

"All clients deserve a full and comprehensive plan; therefore, all engagements require a certain amount of the team's effort. Once client's assets under management reach $500,000, we significantly reduce fees because the additional assets do not add complexity at the same rate at which many fee structures charge. We believe this fee structure creates a fair set up for clients of all sizes which we know to be extremely competitive in the marketplace."

Flat-Fee Financial Planning

For clients earlier in their financial journey, select LiveWell Capital offices offer flat-fee comprehensive financial planning — a dedicated engagement providing rigorous, ongoing planning support. Once investable assets reach $500,000, clients transition to our AUM-based advisory model.

01

Comprehensive Planning Engagement

A structured planning relationship covering cash flow, tax strategy, insurance, estate coordination, and retirement projections — built around your complete financial picture, not just your portfolio.

02

Ongoing Plan Maintenance

Plans are living documents. As your life changes — new income, business events, family transitions — your plan is updated and stress-tested to keep your strategy current and your decisions confident.

03

Coordination Across Advisors

We work alongside your CPA, attorney, and other professionals to ensure your financial plan, tax strategy, and legal documents are all aligned and working together on your behalf.
